newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-GAMES SCHEDULED FOR THIS WEEKEND IN THE SPANISH LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GAMES SCHEDULED FOR THIS WEEKEND IN THE SPANISH LEAGUE.

text.p: The following matches are being played in the Spanish league championship this weekend: (league positions in parentheses, all kickoff times GMT):
Playing Saturday:
Celta (13) vs Atletico Madrid (6) kick-off 1930 gmt

Atletico defender Toni Munoz is struggling to shake off a leg injury after scoring a fine individual goal in the midweek Cup win over Compostela. Celta are just three points away from the relegation zone, and badly need a win against the champions.
playing Sunday:
Compostela (16) vs Tenerife (10) 1600

After going down 2-0 to Betis in midweek Cup action Tenerife will need to rely on their strong away form to strangle the revival of a Compostela side still smarting from a decisive refereeing error in their own Cup defeat at Atletico Madrid.
Logrones (18) vs Zaragoza (21) 1600
Several thousand Zaragoza fans are expected to accompany new coach Luis Costa and their team to Logrones for a crunch game in both team' struggle against relegation.
Sevilla (19) vs Real Sociedad (5) 1600

For the first time in months a Sevilla home game will not begin with a protest against the club president, who has decided not to turn up to the match in which Sevilla will be without injured defenders Juan Martagon and Manuel Jimenez.
Valencia (11) vs Racing Santander (8) 1600

Valencia have been hit by a crisis in defence, with Javi Navarro injured and Francisco Camarasa waiting for a decision on his appeal against suspension. Racing will be without overlapping full-back Javi Navarro, who is suspended.
Barcelona (2) vs Oviedo (12) 1600

Oviedo travel to Barcelona with defenders Mitko Stojkovski and Antonio Rivas doubtful because of injuries for a game which will tell whether Barcelona were boosted or exhausted by Thursday's Cup victory over Real Madrid.
Valladolid (9) vs Rayo Vallecano (14) 1600

Both teams have lost their way after fine starts. Valladolid will have to fill the gap left by the absence of four players, amongst them Croatian striker Alen Peternac, who has a dislocated shoulder and will be replaced by Victor Fernandez.
Sporting Gijon (17) vs Espanyol (15) 1600

Espanyol have been hit by an injury crisis in midfield by losing veteran captain Francisco Lopez and Croatian playmaker Nenad Pralija ahead of a game between two sides that are both uncomfortably close to the relegation zone.
Athletic Bilbao (7) vs Real Betis (3) 1600
Athletic will be put to the test by a Betis side still unbeaten away from home, but likely to start without Yugoslav midfielder Albert Nadj, who was injured in the midweek Cup win over Tenerife.
Real Madrid (1) vs Deportivo Coruna (4) 1830

Real have won the fixture in the past three seasons, but will have to recover quickly from the Cup defeat at Barcelona. Deportivo, with only one victory in the Bernabeu, have been five games without a win and are immersed in internal squabbling.
Playing Monday:
Extremadura (22) vs Hercules (20) 1600
A vital game for two sides that are recovering from appalling starts. Hercules will miss injured Peruvian forward Flavio Maestri, while Extremadura may be without strikers Jose Soler and Carlos Dure.
